Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev sits down with DJ Vlad to break down the chaos behind the 2021 GameStop short squeeze, from Roaring Kitty’s YouTube momentum to retail investor FOMO and Wall Street hedge funds caught in massive short positions. Tenev explains how nostalgia for GameStop, AMC, Hertz and other COVID-hit companies fueled a “people’s bailout,” while Ryan Cohen’s success with Chewy helped shape investor hopes for a turnaround.

As GameStop’s price exploded, Robinhood became the No. 1 app in the App Store, surpassing Instagram and TikTok, while its systems faced unprecedented trading volume. Tenev details the 5 a.m. call from Robinhood’s Florida operations team demanding billions in firm collateral under post-2008 financial regulations, forcing restrictions on certain stocks. He also addresses public anger, “GameStopped” backlash, and accusations involving Citadel, saying communication failures helped drive the controversy.

In this VladTV interview, Chicago rapper Memo600 reflects on the loss of his younger brother Lil Steve, who was killed just days after his birthday, and the unresolved pain that followed. Memo speaks candidly with Vlad about Scrap from MOB being charged and later acquitted in the case, why he says he never wanted anyone sent to prison, and how he views street justice, grief, and accountability years later. He also reveals that his mother spoke with the mother of the man accused of killing Lil Steve, describing an emotional moment of shared loss involving Ruger, Scrap’s older brother. Memo discusses how Steve Drive was named in his brother’s memory, the impact of young teens caught in Chicago violence, and his early connection to Chief Keef, who was once his neighbor and dated his sister. A raw conversation on family, tragedy, drill music history, and growing up in Chicago.

--------
In this VladTV interview, former mob figure Vincent Marino reacts to the 2018 prison killing of Boston crime boss James “Whitey” Bulger at USP Hazelton. Marino discusses Bulger’s path through federal facilities including Tucson, Arizona, Coleman in Florida, and Hazelton, describing how prison politics, informant status, and Bureau of Prisons decisions shaped the danger around him. Vlad notes that Fotios “Freddy” Geas, an American mobster tied to the Springfield faction of the Genovese crime family, was accused in Bulger’s death. Marino also shares his view of Bulger’s legacy, calling him an FBI informant and alleging he was a serial killer, girl killer, pedophile, and “rat.” The conversation examines organized crime codes, federal protection, Boston underworld history, and why many inmates saw Bulger’s murder as “poetic justice.” Watch for Marino’s firsthand prison perspective on one of the most notorious mob deaths in modern U.S. history.

--------
Former Delta Force operator Dale Comstock sits down with VladTV to discuss why he believes some so-called conspiracy theories later prove to be real. Drawing on his military background and government experience, Comstock calls the COVID era a “psyop” and argues it functioned as a test of public compliance, citing his views on PCR testing, vaccines, masking, survival rates, and government incentives. He also revisits Desert Storm, Iraq, Saddam Hussein, weapons of mass destruction, a Department of Veterans Affairs letter about possible chemical exposure, and what he says he witnessed in Baghdad under Hussein’s regime.

The conversation expands into terrorism, Israel, Dubai, Oman, human nature, power, money, masculinity, MMA training, and why Comstock says people should challenge official narratives without blindly accepting consensus. A wide-ranging VladTV interview on war, politics, COVID, sovereignty, and the mindset of a longtime special operations veteran.

Marine veteran Cody Alford joins Vlad to reflect on the true cost of war, questioning why 18- and 19-year-olds can be sent into combat before they’re old enough to legally drink. Alford discusses Iran, the Israel-Palestine debate, October 7th, “Free Palestine,” and how media narratives shape public opinion around global conflicts. He also emphasizes that war creates veterans, casualties, and trauma that institutions like the VA are often unprepared to handle.

The conversation also highlights veteran care, including Craigslist founder Craig Newmark’s major philanthropic support for military families and vets. Alford shares resources connected to Core Medical and Vet Claims, while urging Americans to focus on mental health, community, and issues at home. From Los Angeles to San Diego, Vlad and Cody explore what civilians often miss when debating war from a distance.
